claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a hierarchical heterostructure featuring multilevel chemical fluctuations.
The proposed method integrates machine-learning modeling, first-principles calculations, and CALPHAD.
The method is intended for HfNbTiVAl10 in its reported hierarchical-heterostructured state.
The method is applicable under standard tensile and fracture testing conditions.
Chemical fluctuations and the hierarchical heterostructure mediate the predicted behavior.
Machine-learning modeling can efficiently process large datasets.
Machine-learning modeling can identify patterns relevant to property prediction.
First-principles calculations and CALPHAD provide accurate thermophysical parameters.
First-principles calculations and CALPHAD provide phase-diagram information.
The integrated method will improve prediction of Young's modulus for HfNbTiVAl10.
The integrated method will improve prediction of yield strength for HfNbTiVAl10.
The integrated method will improve prediction of toughness for HfNbTiVAl10.
Prior methods used thermophysical-parameter calculations, CALPHAD, first-principles calculations, or machine-learning modeling separately.
The method ceases to be reliable when alloy composition deviates significantly from the reported state.
The method ceases to be reliable when alloy structure deviates significantly from the reported hierarchical heterostructure.
Prediction reliability is limited by the quality and quantity of training data.
Prediction reliability is limited by the accuracy of the first-principles and CALPHAD calculations.
